Cons:

Description: The SLM Sherpa Micro is Lettucehead3D's SLM metal-printed version of the Sherpa Micro RC2, using the 6T motor variant. Name: SLM Sherpa Micro

Smallest and lightest extruder in the SLM lineup
Direct from Lettucehead3D — quality-controlled production

Verdict Label: Galileo 2 as an Orbiter / Sherpa Mini drop-in — still in public beta
Name: Galileo 2 Standalone
Pros: Same G2E kit parts and motor as the G2E, just different printed parts; drop-in replacement for Orbiter 2.0 or Sherpa Mini; described by Fabreeko as lightweight, comparable to the Orbiter 2.0

Cons:
This is a gear assembly, not a complete extruder — requires a compatible extruder body
Higher cost than standard BMG gear replacements
Limited to specific extruder body compatibility
Most builders won't need this vs standard Annex/Bondtech gear kits
Description: NOTE: The RIDGA v2 is an OEM gear assembly kit, not a complete extruder. Reversed Integrated Drive Gear Assembly v2 by Bondtech. Designed as an upgrade/replacement for standard BMG-style dual-drive gear sets used in extruders like the Sherpa Mini. Features an improved reversed idler geometry for better filament engagement and reduced eccentricity. Compatible with 8T or 10T motor pinion gears. Drive type: Dual. Used as an upgrade in: Sherpa Mini, custom builds. Ecosystem: Universal.
Verdict Label: Bondtech's precision dual-drive gear assembly — an upgrade kit, not a standalone extruder.
Name: RIDGA v2
Pros:
Bondtech precision-machined hardened steel gears
Improved reversed idler geometry vs standard BMG
Compatible with 8T and 10T motor gears
Drop-in upgrade for Sherpa Mini and BMG-style extruders
All-metal construction — no plastic gear components

Cons:
Brand needs adding in Airtable (LDO is not a choice)
Filastruder's modular variants are cheaper than Fabreeko's complete unit — check what's included
Integrated electronics mean a proprietary board
Hotend is not a standard V6/Revo pattern
Description: LDO's Smart Orbiter v3.0 is an all-in-one dual-drive extruder and hotend with integrated Klipper-optimised electronics (filament sensing, auto load/unload, RGB LED). Plated copper heat-block with 72 W ceramic heater and Bondtech CHT nozzle; 175 g overall. Price is for the complete unit with motor and CHT nozzle (Fabreeko).
Verdict Label: All-in-one extruder with integrated electronics — the smartest Orbiter yet
Name: Orbiter 3.0
Pros:
All-in-one extruder + hotend with integrated electronics (filament sensor, auto load/unload)
Only 175 g complete
72 W ceramic heater with plated copper block and CHT nozzle
Klipper-optimised
Quiet Delrin planetary gears

Cons: Heavy at 310g; expensive ($200-225 list, $199.99 at KB-3D); no tension adjustment - fixed gear only; clearance / sold out at Fabreeko ($99 clearance, regular $199.99), so availability is limited
Description: CNC-machined aluminum body extruder with monolithic steel fixed-gear drive. No planetary gearbox — the motor drives directly through a fixed reduction. Rotation distance varies by motor: 7.39 (FXD Pro Motor), 5.29 (Moons N14 10T), 4.23 (LDO 8T N14). Premium build quality targeting high-cycle precision printing.
Verdict Label: Fixed-gear CNC brute - heavy, niche, uncompromising
Name: FXD v1.1
Pros: CNC-machined aluminium body; monolithic hardened steel gears (60-64 HRC surface); fixed-gear drive with no springs or levers to slip; 100% constrained filament path - handles 60A and softer flexibles without grinding; very high pushing force

Cons:
175g including standard hotend - heavier than Orbiter V2.5 (135g)
70C max operating temperature at 0.55A RMS motor current
Mellow/LDO implementation of the Orbiter design - support via reseller rather than Orbiter Projects
Description: Orbiter v3.5 represents the next step in the evolution of the proven Orbiter v3.0, with several improvements for enhanced performance and reliability, including reduced fan noise, improved filament sensing, improved tolerances, and expanded hotend compatibility. It is a compact all-in-one direct-drive extruder with a 12mm dual-drive system, integrated filament sensing and automatic unload, and a front heatsink compatible with the LDO hotend with TFN nozzle and the E3D Revo ecosystem.
Verdict Label: Proven Orbiter V3.5 dual-drive with LDO motor and smart filament sensing - a safe direct-drive pick for Voron and Ender/CR-10 builds.
Name: Smart Orbiter V3.5
Pros:
Dual-drive 12mm gear system with 6.5kg+ extrusion force
Smart filament sensor with reduced false runout detections
10dB quieter fan than V3.0; knurled main shaft for precise extrusion
LDO motor included; plug-and-play for Voron 2.4 / Ender3 / CR-10

Cons: No complete kit: printed parts plus the LDO G2E donor kit; assembled weight unpublished
Description: Combines the proven 9:1 planetary gearing from the Galileo 2 with the Orbiter 2 mounting footprint. Designed by @bythorsthunder, repository maintained by tetsu97. A bridge between two popular extruder families — useful when your toolhead has an Orbiter mount but you want planetary reduction.
Verdict Label: Galileo 2 guts in a standalone Orbiter-mount extruder
Name: WristWatch G2
Pros: 9:1 planetary gearbox with large 16mm drive gear; Orbiter 2 mounting pattern fits XOL, A4T and other toolheads; only 3 printed parts

Cons:
No published assembled weight
Dated design next to Revo/Orbiter rivals
Single-drive only
Full kit motor is the older Compact But Powerful unit
Mirrored and standard versions are separate SKUs
Description: E3D's classic all-metal direct-drive combo — Titan extruder and V6 hotend in one compact unit, rated to 285 °C with 3:1 gearing and a standard NEMA17 mounting pattern. Great for flexibles thanks to its short, constrained filament path; the full kit includes the Compact But Powerful motor.
Verdict Label: The classic V6 + Titan combo in one compact unit — proven, if dated
Name: Titan Aero
Pros:
Proven V6 + Titan combination in one rigid unit
Extra 25 mm of Z height vs separate V6 + Titan
3:1 gearing pairs with a compact motor
Short filament path suits flexibles
Standard NEMA17 mounting pattern

Cons:
Older design than Orbiter V3.5 - noisier fan, no RGB sensor board
Sensor adds wiring and Klipper/Marlin configuration
135g plus sensor weight - heavier than the lightest modern extruders
Description: The Orbiter Extruder V2.5 features a robust injection-molded outer shell, enhancing durability. It utilizes an LDO high-temperature motor for strong torque output and improved performance. The high-quality, RNC nano-coated gears (HRC60+) incorporate an innovative flat-bottom design, maintaining consistent extrusion rates regardless of filament position.
Verdict Label: The classic LDO Orbiter V2.5 plus a smart filament sensor - proven dual-drive extrusion with runout detection.
Name: Orbiter V2.5 + Smart Filament Sensor
Pros:
Proven Orbiter V2.5 design with 40% more pushing force than V2.0
RNC nano-coated hardened gears (HRC60+) for abrasive filaments
Smart filament sensor with steel-ball switch reduces false runouts
LDO high-temperature motor included

Cons: Work in progress per the README and CAD was not yet published; no commercial kit; no verified current seller of a complete Orbiter v2.0 donor kit (West3D delisted it); assembled weight unpublished
Description: A direct drive extruder for the Voron V0.1 that uses the guts of an Orbiter v2.0. Shares the Mini-AfterSherpa mounting pattern with the RoundHouse and was designed to complement the 5015 Toolhead.
Verdict Label: Orbiter-v2.0-guts direct-drive extruder for the Voron V0.1 — still a work in progress
Name: RoundAbout
Pros: Reuses the Orbiter v2.0 gear set (7.5:1); Mini-AfterSherpa mount, designed to complement the 5015 toolhead; direct drive for the V0.1

Cons:
Coldside only — hotside, heater and sensor sold separately
No published coldside-only weight
1.75 mm only
123-3D lists the coldside kit as end of life
Description: Compact Revo coldside kit — 92 g lighter and 11 mm shorter than the classic Hemera, with the same 3.32:1 dual-drive gearing and T-slot mounting. Pairs with any Revo or V6 hotside (sold separately); stalls instead of stripping filament on a jam.
Verdict Label: Lighter, shorter Hemera with Revo quick-change — the modern pick
Name: Hemera XS
Pros:
92 g lighter and 11 mm shorter than the classic Hemera
Revo quick-change nozzles with the right hotside
Stalls instead of stripping filament on jams
Built-in PTC safety behaviour
T-slot mounting

Cons:
Requires HGX-Lite gear kit — additional cost on top of printed parts
Smaller community install base vs Sherpa Mini or Orbiter
Printed plastic body — less rigid than CNC alternatives
Fewer pre-built toolhead integrations than LGX Lite or Sherpa
Description: Print-it-yourself compact direct drive extruder by nhchiu (also the designer of ProtoXtruder). Uses HGX-Lite large drive gears (44:10, 37:17 ratio) in a compact body with the same mounting footprint as the Bondtech LGX Lite. Features a thickened idler arm vs original design to prevent flex under load. Supports 3 types of 4mm OD PTFE tube retainers. Available on Printables and GitHub (nhchiu/VoronMods). Drive type: Dual (HGX-Lite gears). Ecosystem: Voron / CoreXY.
Verdict Label: Free-to-print LGX Lite-footprint extruder using HGX-Lite gears — strong dual-drive grip, zero cost beyond the gear kit.
Name: Hummingbird
Pros:
LGX Lite mounting footprint — wide toolhead compatibility
HGX-Lite gears provide strong dual-drive grip at high ratio
Thickened idler arm prevents flex under sustained load
Print-it-yourself — zero cost beyond HGX-Lite gear kit
By nhchiu — active Voron community contributor (ProtoXtruder designer)

Cons:
Own mounting pattern — needs a printed adapter for most toolheads
Relatively new design with a smaller user base than Bondtech/E3D rivals
Hotend parts are Phaetus-specific
Description: Compact dual-drive extruder from Phaetus with a 5.8:1 gear ratio and an integrated filament break sensor. RNC II coated drive gears deliver 70 N+ of pushing force; 160 g including motor. Mounts via its own pattern, with Voron adapters available on GitHub.
Verdict Label: High-torque dual-drive value with a built-in filament sensor
Name: Apus 2
Pros:
Integrated filament break sensor
70 N+ pushing force from RNC II coated dual-drive gears
160 g including motor — light for a direct-drive unit
5.8:1 gearing gives fine extrusion control

Cons:
Newer product with smaller community install base
Limited documentation compared to Sherpa Mini
Niche form factor — most builders don't need this slim profile
Description: The Lite Pro Slim Repack is Lettucehead3D's production version of the Lite Pro extruder in a slimmed-down repackaged form factor. Designed for toolhead builds where standard extruder body depth is a constraint.
Verdict Label: A slim, high-ratio compact extruder for space-constrained toolheads — Lettucehead3D's production repack.
Name: Lite Pro Slim Repack
Pros:
Slim profile fits tight toolhead designs
Production quality from Lettucehead3D
High gear ratio for increased extrusion torque
Lightweight design reduces toolhead moving mass

Cons: $150 is expensive vs. community alternatives; heavier than plastic-body LGX Lite; overkill for non-heated-chamber builds
Description: The all-CNC aluminum version of the Bondtech LGX Lite. Eliminates body flex under high acceleration or elevated chamber temperatures. Same gear ratio and LGX Lite mount compatibility makes it a direct upgrade from the standard LGX Lite. The practical choice when printing at sustained high temps where a plastic body would creep or deform. Gear Ratio: 9.576:1 is the overall reduction from the published gear pairs 44:10 and 37:17 (the previous 44:10 was only the first stage).
Verdict Label: Premium LGX Lite — CNC aluminum for heated chamber and high-speed builds
Name: LGX Lite PRO
Pros: CNC aluminum body eliminates plastic flex under heat or high acceleration; same gear ratio and LGX Lite mount as the standard LGX Lite; direct drop-in upgrade; Bondtech reliability and support
